# mtgish RON execution progress

## Run 2026-10-03: P0-INVENTORY

Status: complete semantic inventory/reporting slice. Scope/instance prerequisites
remain unfinished; this run does not start another slice. The working tree began
with staged skill deletions, changes to engine/registry/docs, and untracked RON
sources, compiler, loader, design, and local scripts. These were preserved.

### Contract and dependencies

`InspectFS(fs.FS, string) (*Inventory, error)` reports every parsed AST node,
including descendants of unsupported parents. CLI:
`go run ./cmd/loadcards -inventory -json`. The strict loader still determines
CLI success, so inventory cannot make a rejected collection acceptable.

Dependencies: existing `Parse`, `Compile`, `Node`, `Position`, `Issue`,
`definitionKey`, and `LoadFS`. Engine reuse is unchanged: existing factory,
action, target, damage, zone, and registry services execute accepted cards.
No new engine rules, runtime registry, Go-card fallback, or DSL deletion is part
of this slice. CR 608.2b/c/n describes the spell regression's target, resolution,
and final graveyard handling; the slice does not change these rules.

Schema, exact role table, shape/context rules, paths, and API limits:
[mtgish-ron-inventory.md](mtgish-ron-inventory.md), implemented in
`pkg/mage/dsl/ron/inventory.go`. Shapes group immediate argument kinds/names
and sorted fields. Context keeps constructor/argument paths and removes only
list indices. Known roles come from parent contracts; descendants of unknown
contracts remain explicitly unknown. All expression support is unverified.
Engine-validation and behavior-verification counts are null, not zero.

Supported reporting contexts are all symbols, literals, lists, tuples, and
structs, in every parsed card and nested expression. Role adapters cover:

| Parent role and exact shape | Argument roles |
| --- | --- |
| card `Card` named fields | `Rules`: rule; other fields: metadata |
| metadata | metadata descendants |
| rule `SpellActions/1`, `Activated/2`, `TriggerA/2` | actions; cost/actions; event/actions |
| rule `EnchantPermanent/1`, `EachPermanentLayerEffect/2`, `PermanentLayerEffect/2` | permanent filter; filter/static modification; permanent reference/static modification |
| actions `Targeted/2`, `ActionList/1` | target/actions; action |
| target `TargetPermanent/1`, `TargetPlayer/1`, `TargetSpell/1` | permanent/player/spell filter |
| cost `And/1`, `TapPermanent/1`, `SacrificePermanent/1`, `PayMana/1` | cost; permanent reference; permanent reference; metadata |
| action single-permanent tap/untap/destroy/destroy-no-regen/regenerate/sacrifice `/1` | permanent reference |
| action `PlayerAction/2`, `SpellDealsDamage/3`, `PermanentDealsDamage/3` | player reference/player action; spell reference/value/recipient; permanent reference/value/recipient |
| action or player action draw-number/gain-life/lose-life `/1` | value |
| permanent filter `And/1`, `Or/1`, `SinglePermanent/1` | permanent filter; permanent filter; permanent reference |
| event enter/die/upkeep `/1` | permanent filter; permanent filter; player filter |
| player filter `SinglePlayer/1` | player reference |
| list, any role | same element role |
| other forms | unknown descendants, fully walked |

Unknown-field validation in `compiler.go` now selects fields in sorted order.
A repeated invalid-declaration test first failed with `UnknownZ` instead of
`UnknownA`; the sorting repair makes the diagnostic deterministic.

All 12 source files were parsed and walked in full: 2,445 records, 986 unique
card names, 72,938 AST node occurrences, and 8,528 context/shape signatures.
23,096 node occurrences have unknown roles. This larger signature count includes
literals, list envelopes, and context; it is not comparable to the snapshot's
600 tuple signatures. Reporting coverage now includes every parsed node.

Strict loader before and after: **836 compiled records, 1,609 rejected records**.
There are 243 unique compiled names and 743 rejected names in this collection.
Compilation gain: zero. Newly supported gameplay cards: zero. The reporting
slice affects all 986 unique cards without changing their RON records.

## Run 2026-10-03: P0-SCOPE-PLAYER

Status: complete single-player target/read prerequisite slice. P0-SCOPE remains
partial. This run stops here; it does not start player-scoped life actions.

### Contract, dependencies, and reuse

Exact supported signatures/contexts are recorded in
[mtgish-ron-player-scopes.md](mtgish-ron-player-scopes.md).
`TargetPlayer(AnyPlayer)/1` inside a single-element `Targeted/2` declaration
produces a typed player declaration. `PlayerAction/2` accepts symbol `You` or
symbol `Ref_TargetPlayer`; `DrawNumberCards/1` accepts the existing `Integer/1`
or announced spell `ValueX` value forms. Direct draws retain the resolving
controller. The existing spell, activation, and supported trigger action builders
share this lowering. Nested/multiple declarations remain errors.

`playerTargetPlan` gives a player declaration an immutable lexical identity.
`playerReferencePlan` reads that identity or the resolving controller.
`instanceBindings` maps the identity to a fresh engine player target for each
factory/action build. Effect factories now receive this instance environment
instead of only a permanent binding. Permanent binding behavior is retained.
Player draws use `mage.DrawFor`, `mage.ValueAtResolution`, and
`mage.DeclarePlayerTarget`; `mage.WithTargets` normalizes typed declarations.
Engine definition validation now sees the target read and can reject a missing
declaration. No chosen state, registered Go factory, or card-name branch is
stored in the compiler plan.

Dependencies: existing parser, compiler action plans, typed player targets,
resolving contexts, draw actions, definition validation, stack copy/retargeting,
game clones, and transactional casting. All required engine contracts exist;
no engine implementation changes are needed. RON owns the player spelling and
scope rejection. Relevant existing rules are CR 113.7a and 608.2b/c/n.
No permanent LKI query, phasing operation, replacement ordering, or simultaneous
operation is introduced; the retained engine services still own those rules.

## Run 2026-10-03: P0-SCOPE-PERMANENT-UNARY

Status: complete unary-action prerequisite slice. P0-SCOPE remains partial.
This run stops here; temporary layer selectors and damage references remain open.

### Contract, dependencies, and reuse

Exact signatures, supported contexts, complete-record audit, and reference
lifetimes are in [mtgish-ron-permanent-scopes.md](mtgish-ron-permanent-scopes.md).
The six unary actions `DestroyPermanent/1`, `DestroyPermanentNoRegen/1`,
`TapPermanent/1`, `UntapPermanent/1`, `RegeneratePermanent/1`, and
`SacrificePermanent/1` now lower typed permanent references in the existing
spell, activation, and trigger action-list contexts. Symbols are
`Ref_TargetPermanent` in a single permanent declaration, `ThisPermanent` for a
permanent source, and `HostPermanent` for an Aura source. Source/host/target
reads have separate typed plans; permanent target declarations have immutable
lexical identities and fresh per-instance engine bindings. Invalid syntax,
types, missing declarations, cross-rule reads, and unsupported event references
remain compilation errors. Engine definition validation now sees all six reads.

Dependency: P0-SCOPE-PLAYER's per-instance effect environment, existing target
normalization, parser, action-list compiler, and engine typed permanent refs.
Reuse: `DeclarePermanentTarget`, `This`, `AttachedPermanent`, `Destroy`,
`DestroyWithoutRegeneration`, `TapSubject`, `UntapPermanent`, `Regenerate`,
`Sacrifice`, definition validation, stack target/copy services, game clones,
retained source attachments, regeneration/replacement execution, and
transactional activation costs. All needed engine contracts exist; no engine
implementation change is needed. RON owns spelling and scope checks. CR 113.7a,
400.7, 608.2b/c/h/n, and 702.26b/d/g supply identity, timing, LKI, legality,
and phasing contracts. No saved characteristic reader or simultaneous batch is
introduced, and replacement ordering remains the shared engine's contract.

### Nested forms, affected cards, and source findings

Fresh whole-collection AST inspection covers descendants after first errors.
All nested occurrences of the six names were inspected, including separate cost
roles and unknown contexts. Complete distinct RON records were read for the 92
cards with direct action occurrences. The companion document lists every card,

Newly accepted cards: **Regeneration** (six identical reprints), **The Brute**

The engine's retained attachment service supplies this exact behavior.

No data defect was corrected, and no RON asset changed. Fresh inventory file
hashes match all 12 vocabulary snapshot hashes, so no source snapshot refresh
is needed. The Gaea's Liege/Fastbond concerns remain outside this slice.
There was no environment failure. Missing adapters were resolved in `ron`;
no missing engine service was found.

New engine signature:
`AnimateEach(PermanentSet, int, int, ...core.Color) StaticRule`, installed by
`Static`. The service adds Creature in layer 4, optionally sets color in layer
5, and sets base P/T in layer 7b. The effect manager retains selected incarnation
references for one layer cycle (CR 613.6), including after type addition or
layer-6 source ability removal, then selects current membership on the next
application. Rule/source identities keep instances distinct. Cloned effect
managers have independent cycle state. The new service tests membership-changing
type dependencies on isolated game/effect clones and uses the existing sorter.
This does not establish complete dependency support for all engine effects.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

Private signatures:

- `compileOptionalUntap(Node) (optionFactory, error)` supports only rule
  `PermanentRuleEffect/2` with symbol `ThisPermanent` and a list containing
  exactly symbol `MayChooseNotToUntapDuringUntap`.
- `compileTappedUpkeep(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)` supports only rule
  `TriggerI/3`, event `AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(You))`,
  condition `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, IsTapped)`, and an action
  declaration accepted by the shared action compiler. Each constructor has its
  exact tuple arity; source/player/filter operands are symbols.

Both rules require a permanent card context. Spell, cost and action contexts,
wrong arity, tuple-shaped symbols, other subjects, filters, events and mixed
optional untap operations remain declaration errors. General PermanentRuleEffect
and TriggerI families remain partial.

Optional untap lowers to `Static(While(condition,
GrantKeywordModification(This, AttrMayNotUntap)))` with an unconditional typed
battlefield condition. It grants the attribute through the existing ability
layer so ability removal disables it. The trigger lowers to
`At(YourUpkeep, Sequence(actions...), WithInterveningIf(PermanentIsTapped(This)))`.
Its action targets are added from the same freshly built action plan. No mutable
choice is captured in a compiled factory. Per-instance target/cost bindings and
source incarnations remain owned by existing engine services.

Engine reuse: native land play, tapped entry, untap-step player decisions and
restrictions, layer/ability lifecycle, YourUpkeep, typed state conditions,
intervening-if detection and resolution checks, source incarnations, event and
pending-trigger services, stack copies/countering, phasing, control changes,
cloning, counter addition, typed chosen-counter payment, immediate mana ability
resolution and transactional rollback. RON owns spelling, shape validation,
inventory roles and lowering. No engine rule/API changed; no card-name branch,
Go-card fallback, global last-action slot, declaration panic or parallel rules
service was added. Relevant contracts read: CR 400.7, 502.1/3/4, 503.1a,
603.3/4, 605.1a/3b and 702.26b–d, with API and engine rules-contract docs.
No new LKI-characteristic query, replacement ordering or simultaneous batch
operation was introduced; existing engine behavior remains the reuse boundary.

actions, and PermanentPassesFilter condition operands as permanent_reference /

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Exact shape/context contract: [mtgish-ron-next-untap.md](mtgish-ron-next-untap.md).
`compileEffect(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)` accepts action tuple
`PermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextUntap/1`. The operand must be an
in-scope symbol accepted by `compilePermanentRef(Node, scope)`:
`ThisPermanent`, Aura `HostPermanent`, or declared `Ref_TargetPermanent`.
The shared action compiler supports spells, activations, modifier-bearing
activations and supported trigger actions. It rejects wrong arity, tuple
references, wrong roles, unbound/wrong-type/cross-rule reads. General static
untap prohibitions and collection actions remain unsupported.

Lowering reuses `mage.SkipNextUntap(subject.build(instanceBindings))` in the
existing unary permanent action builder. Fresh typed target declarations give
each factory/action its own reads. Immutable plans store no selected state.
RON owns spelling, scope, diagnostics and inventory operand roles; mage owns
resolution, legality, source incarnations, Aura attachment/departure LKI,
turn restriction storage/expiration, control, phasing, copies and clones.
Payment still uses the existing transactional activation path. No engine API
or rule changed; no fallback, card-name branch, global action slot, declaration
panic, partial registry or parallel subsystem was added.

The restriction starts at resolution. It neither taps the subject nor prevents
other untap effects. The next untap step of the current controller consumes it,
even when the subject is untapped. Repeated applications expire together.
Control changes do not capture the old controller. Phasing after installation
preserves the restriction; absent/phased subjects cannot receive it. Departure
clears it, and return cannot redirect a pending typed reference. Read contracts:
engine doc.go, composable permanent-reference/SkipNextUntap services, turn
execution/TurnSystem, definition validation, DSL/API and rules-contract docs;
CR 400.7, 502.1/3/4, 608.2b and 702.26b/d. No new LKI characteristic query,
replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation contract is introduced.

retained symbol `MayChooseNotToUntapDuringUntap`. This is a top-level permanent
rule context only. It rejects tuple spellings, bad arity/lists, mixed operations,
unbound targets, host/player reads, costs/actions, instant/sorcery rules, and
conditional wrappers. Diagnostics now describe self untap sources/operations
because the compiler is no longer limited to optional untap.

The immutable plan captures only `core.Attr`; each factory call creates its own
`mage.Static(mage.While(condition,
mage.GrantKeywordModification(mage.This, attribute)))` ability. The condition
uses the existing pure StateConditionFunc with StateBattlefield dependency.
RON owns spelling, shape validation and lowering. The engine owns static source
lifetime, ability layers, current control, phase-in, untap selection, transactional
payments, copies, incarnation identity and clones. Existing source references
are typed `mage.This`, with no mutable choices shared by compiler factories.
Inventory already assigns permanent_rule_operation to this list; no role adapter

### Exact supported contract and ownership

Capability P7-GLOBAL-LANDWALK-BLOCKING is complete for this exact shape/context:

- Top-level permanent rule tuple `EachPermanentRuleEffect/2`.
- Filter tuple `And/1` containing a list of exactly `IsCardtype(Creature)` and
  `HasAbility(Landwalk(IsLandType(subtype)))`, in either order.
- Operation list containing exactly tuple `CanBeBlockedAsThoughItDidntHave/1`
  with `Landwalk(IsLandType(subtype))`; the subtype must match the filter.
- Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest and Desert operands are supported.

Private signatures: `compileLandwalkBlockingRule(Node) (optionFactory, error)`
and `validateGlobalLandwalkFilter(Node, core.Attr) error`. `compileRule` delegates
this family to the new adapter. RON owns spelling, arity/kind validation,
filter-operation compatibility, diagnostics and inventory roles. It captures
only an immutable core.Attr and constructs a fresh effect per factory call.
There are no chosen bindings, targets, costs or mutable declaration instances
in this shape. Existing `WithStaticAbility(NullifyLandwalkEffect(keyword))`
provides the exact global rules behavior, source lifetime, clone isolation and
ability-removal handling. Blocking checks use HasLandwalkEvasion with CanBlock;
the landwalk keyword stays on the creature and other evasion remains active.

The guard rejects narrower filters because the reused engine rule is global.
It does not silently discard controller/color/source restrictions. Other
EachPermanentRuleEffect operations, arbitrary landwalk filters, temporary or
self-only contexts remain unsupported. No global last-action slot, card-name
branch, Go fallback, runtime declaration panic or partial production registry
was added. No engine service was changed. No new LKI, cost rollback,
replacement-order or simultaneous-operation contract applies to this static
shape. CR 509.1b, 702.14a-e, 604.2, 400.7 and 702.26b/d were consulted.

Capability P2-CHOOSE-ONE-SPELL-MODES is complete for
`SpellActions(Modal_ChooseOne([mode, mode, ...]))` on instants and sorceries.
The constructor has one positional list argument and at least two modes.
Each mode uses the existing supported ActionList/1 or Targeted/2 action-plan
shape, with at most one target declaration. Every mode body must compile.

Targeted_Modal remain errors. Unsupported actions do not become accepted

Private adapter signature:
`compileModalSpell(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
`scope.targetNamespace string` supplies distinct internal declaration names
(`mode1/Ref_TargetPermanent`, etc.). RON spelling and lexical reads remain
unchanged. `compileTarget(Node, scope) (targetFactory, string, error)` uses
that namespace for permanent, player and spell declarations; its existing
callers have an empty namespace and retain their names. Each mode clears
inherited target plans, compiles independently, and builds fresh declarations
and effects inside each factory call. Plans capture no chosen state.

`actionPlan.build` and typed target bindings supply the existing group mapping.
`mage.NewModalSpell` receives mode targets/effects and labels from effect
sequence text with readable target names. Existing engine services choose mode/targets at announcement,
pay costs transactionally, keep mode/targets on the stack, recheck legality,
resolve only the chosen body, and copy/retarget without selecting a new mode.
`CounterSpellRef` and `Destroy` continue to use stack/permanent identity and
shared zone/regeneration services. No engine execution service was added.
There is no Go fallback, card-name branch, mutable shared target state,
last-action slot, partial production registry or game-time declaration panic.
The minimum mode count is checked before factory construction.

permanent-reference argument. Accepted references: symbol `Ref_TargetPermanent`

`compileEffect(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)` builds
`mage.ReturnToHand(subject.build(instanceBindings))`. Per-factory declarations
and action bindings stay fresh; immutable plans capture no chosen game state.

rules, choose-one spell modes, activations and supported triggers. Unsupported
parents such as CreateFutureTrigger remain rejected. The action does not make
those enclosing contexts supported. No source data, public API or engine
execution service changed. This is a missing compiler adapter, not a missing
engine contract, data defect or environment failure.

Reuse: typed permanent references, instanceBindings, definition validation,
transactional casting/activation, stack target checks, modal copies,
ReturnToHand, BouncePermanentToHand, battlefield incarnation identity,
attachment LKI and Game.Clone. Owner is independent of controller; return is
independent of regeneration. An absent/phased object cannot move; phase-in
preserves identity, while departure/return creates a new object. Host reads use
current attachment or the captured departed source's last attachment, and
cannot follow a returned source. Existing rules: CR 400.7, 608.2b, 702.26b,
700.2a/c/f/g. No new simultaneous-operation or replacement-order contract is
introduced. Existing engine token/leave-trigger tests remain green.

### Engine gap and exact supported contract

Missing compiler prerequisite: a typed single mixed recipient declaration/read.
Missing engine prerequisite for future prevention: `DamageSystem` prepares each
simultaneous request in slice order, applying the shared shield immediately.
There is no allocation choice among simultaneous damage sources. CR 615.7 gives
that choice to the affected player or permanent's controller. A temporary,
standalone Go probe used two sources dealing 2 each to one player, one with
lifelink, and a shield of 2. The recipient implemented both ChooseMode and
ChooseDamageDistribution. `go run /tmp/ron-prevention-probe.go` reported
`choice calls=0; source controller life=20; recipient life=18`. Choosing one
prevented damage from each source would instead give the source controller one
life. `dealSimultaneousDamageOutcomes` and `preventionShieldReplacement` confirm
the packet-order consumption. This is engine behavior, not a source defect or
an environment failure. Future prevention remains rejected in production.

Exact supported declaration: symbol `AnyTarget` as the one target in
`Targeted([AnyTarget], ActionList(...))`. Exact read: symbol `Ref_AnyTarget` as
argument 3 of `SpellDealsDamage(ThisSpell, value, Ref_AnyTarget)` or
`PermanentDealsDamage(ThisPermanent, value, Ref_AnyTarget)`. Existing fixed/X
values and spell/activation/trigger action-list contexts remain supported.
Existing spell choose-one modes give each declaration a private namespace.
Multiple groups, numbered recipients, wrapping this mixed reference as a
permanent/player, and unsupported enclosing actions remain rejected.

`compileDamageTargetRef(Node, scope) (*damageTargetPlan, error)` checks the
lexical typed plan. `scope.damageTarget`, `actionPlan.damageTarget` and
`instanceBindings.recipients map[*damageTargetPlan]*mage.DamageTargetBinding`
carry immutable plan identity and fresh per-factory declarations. `compileTarget`
builds `mage.DeclareDamageTarget(namespace+"Ref_AnyTarget")`; action-plan building
includes the declaration with existing typed target groups. The damage body
uses `mage.DealDamageFrom(mage.This, boundRecipient,
mage.ValueAtResolution(amount))`. Mode scopes clear inherited mixed plans.

### Exact shapes, contexts and reuse boundary

- `compileFixedPowerFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)` accepts
  `PowerIs(LessThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)))`,
  `PowerIs(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)))` and `PowerIs(EqualTo(Integer(n)))`.
  Signed integer constants are allowed. Lowering uses `HasPowerLTE`,
  `HasPowerGTE`, `HasPowerEqual`; each query reads current layered power.
  These are permanent filters, including nested And/Or in supported contexts.
  Dynamic values, other comparisons, malformed tuples and bare integers reject.
- `compileTemporaryBlocking(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` accepts only
  `CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(Ref_TargetPermanent, [CantBeBlocked],
  UntilEndOfTurn)` with a declared permanent target in resolving action lists.
  Supported spell, choose-one mode, activation and trigger contexts share the
  adapter. Source/host/result references, other operations, mixed operation
  lists and other durations remain rejected. It uses `compilePermanentRef`,
  per-instance bindings and `Until(EndOfTurn, CantBeBlocked(typedTarget))`.
- Inventory now assigns the rule subject/operation/duration roles and nested
  power comparison/value roles. Role reporting does not claim gameplay support.

RON owns syntax, declaration validation and scope; mage retains all reusable
rules. Existing definition validation, target selection/rechecks, transactional
costs, source LKI, incarnation capture, phasing, combat rules, cleanup, ability
copying and clone services are reused. No engine behavior or public API changed.
Rules read: CR 400.7, 601.2c, 608.2b/h, 611.2c, 514.2 and 702.26b-f.
No new replacement, choice or simultaneous-operation behavior is introduced.
No comments were added to code. API and rules-contract docs describe only the
supported shapes and tested reuse.

### Exact signatures, supported contexts and dependencies

- `PreventUntapDuringStepForMatching(PermanentFilter) ContinuousEffect` is a
  reusable engine static rule. It stores an immutable filter declaration, not
  selected game objects. `matchingUntapRestrictions() map[uuid.UUID]bool` creates
  a local snapshot after phasing and layer evaluation, before the untap loop.
  Active printed-source checks use the existing effect wrapper; final layered
  characteristics use the existing filters. Other untap effects remain legal.
  Recipient ability removal does not erase this restriction. Source departure,
  phasing and ability removal disable it. Source return builds a new instance.
  The existing `PreventUntapForMatching` API and callers remain unchanged.
- `compileCollectionPermanentRule(Node) (optionFactory, error)` accepts
  `EachPermanentRuleEffect(filter, [DoesntUntapDuringControllersUntap])` in
  permanent Rules, with one bare operation and a supported source-independent
  permanent filter. The established landwalk blocking shape delegates to its
  existing adapter. Mixed/empty operation lists, operation tuples, bound/result
  selectors and source-dependent controller collections remain rejected.
- `compileFilter` accepts `IsSupertype(Legendary)` for permanent filters,
  including nested And/Or, using `mage.IsLegendary`. Basic/Snow/World and
  card/spell filter roles remain unsupported. No new supertype engine semantics
  are invented.
- `compileEffect` accepts `TapEachPermanent(filter)` in resolving spell, mode,
  activation and trigger action lists, using
  `mage.TapEach(mage.MatchingPermanents(filter))`. Filters are the supported
  source-independent permanent forms. Target collections, choice results,
  loop bindings and player-dependent selections are not accepted. Selection
  occurs at resolution and uses existing incarnation, phasing and simultaneous
  tap/event services.
- Source-only `WhenAPermanentEntersTheBattlefield(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))`
  now lowers to `mage.WhenEvent(mage.Enters(mage.This), body)`. The typed event
  path keeps event context separate from target declarations. It preserves
  source departure, phasing, return and copies without legacy auto-target fizzle.
- The layer reset now includes `ptSwitched` in its reset condition. The new
  final-power untap test exposed inconsistent repeated switch evaluation.
- Inventory assigns the TapEachPermanent child its permanent_filter role.
  Reporting still marks signature support unverified; no support claim is
  inferred from a signature name.

RON owns syntax and validation; mage owns rule execution. Factory calls build
fresh abilities/effects. Costs, targets, source LKI, incarnation checks, cloning,
continuous layers and tap batches reuse shared engine services. The local untap
snapshot cannot leak into another game or overwrite another binding. No new
payment, replacement, optional-choice or global last-action contract is added.
No Go fallback, card-name dispatch, partial registry or runtime declaration
panic was added.

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

- Existing `mage.DiscardAtRandom(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`
  resolves the player and amount once, then selects distinct cards from a local
  copy of the current hand using `Game.RandIntn`. Selection consumes one value
  per card; empty hands and nonpositive amounts consume none. Short hands limit
  the number selected. A prevented discard does not cause another card to be
  selected or the same card to be selected again.
- The action now calls existing `discardActionsTogether(actions, false)`.
  Effect-caused `DiscardAction` replacements are prepared before any moves;
  moves finish before discard events. Prevented cards do not stop other cards
  or later instructions. Shared replacement ordering/rechecks, destination
  handling, graveyard visits, trackers and event dispatch remain in the engine.
  The public signature, metadata, definition validation and existing callers
  are preserved. Legacy random helpers and random discard costs are unchanged.
- `compileRandomDiscard(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)` accepts bare
  `DiscardACardAtRandom`, `DiscardNumberCardsAtRandom(Integer(n))/1` for n >= 0,
  and `DiscardNumberCardsAtRandom(ValueX)/1` in an announced-X scope. Other
  amounts, singular tuples, malformed declarations and unbound X are rejected.
- Supported contexts are resolving action lists in spells, selected modes,
  activations and already-supported triggers. `PlayerAction(player, action)/2`
  uses `compilePlayerRef`; direct actions keep the resolving controller even
  when the action list declares a player target. Typed target, spell-controller
  and available step/cast event reads use the existing instance environment.
  No new binding kind or mutable compiler state is added.
- The factory lowers to `mage.DiscardAtRandom(ctx.player.build(bindings), amount)`.
  Each factory/action build keeps its own target/event bindings. X uses the
  existing announced resolution value. RON owns spelling, shape rejection and
  lexical scope; mage owns random selection, replacements and movement.
- Inventory gives the plural action's child the value role in action and player
  action contexts, including nested forms under unsupported parents. Reporting
  does not infer verified support from constructor names.

No LKI characteristic read or permanent target is introduced. Pending source
abilities retain their resolving controller/target after departure, return,
control change or phasing through the existing stack/source contracts. Phasing
is not interpreted as a zone change. Random choices remain resolution work;
cost affordability and failed payments do not consume random values. No global
result slot, runtime declaration panic, name branch, fallback or partial
production registry was introduced.

because events saw partial hands and hand-dependent replacements saw a prior

rather than cost discard, it also proved a prevented first card was selected

with a nonempty stack. These fixture repairs preserve legality and all behavior

### Exact supported shape, reuse and defects

`Rampage(integer literal)/1` in a permanent's top-level `Rules` accepts n >= 0.
RON rejects symbols, wrong arity, negative/nonliteral values and action contexts.
Nested ability choices and `AddAbility` grants remain rejected. Inventory assigns
only this rule's argument the `integer_literal` role; nested shapes still report
their existing roles without a support claim. Factories build fresh abilities.

The adapter calls existing `mage.RampageTrigger(int) *GenericTriggered`.
The engine contract needed two repairs: listen to `EvtCreatureBecomesBlocked`
with `EventSourceIsSelf`, rather than the general `EvtBlockersDecl`; and use
`This` plus `Until(EndOfTurn, ModifyPT(...))` instead of an uncaptured UUID boost.
`RampageEffect(int) Effect` and `RampageEffectData` are retained for callers and
ability detection. Existing combat transitions, blocker membership, typed source
incarnations, generic stack/copy/clone services and continuous layers are reused.
Blockers are counted at resolution, as CR 702.23b requires, not at trigger time.
A control change removes the source from combat and thus removes its group.

These are separate missing compiler-adapter and engine-contract gaps. There is
no source-data defect or environment failure in this slice. Gaea's Liege and

be a symbol bound to a single local `TargetPermanent`. Supported resolving
contexts are spells, spell modes, activations and existing supported triggers.

numbered groups, source/host operands, static rules and costs are not added.

`ron` validates wrapper arity, reference kind, lexical binding and context,
then lowers to `mage.DealDamageFrom(mage.This, permanentTargetBinding,
mage.ValueAtResolution(value))`. Existing `compilePermanentRef` and per-factory
`instanceBindings.permanents` supply typed identities. Engine definition
validation can detect a removed target declaration. No engine implementation
or public API changed. Existing announcement, transactional payment, target
filter recheck, incarnation, source LKI, damage, replacement, stack-copy and
clone services own execution. Inventory assigns the wrapper operand the
`permanent_reference` role in known recipient contexts without claiming that
all enclosing contexts compile. No new simultaneous action service is needed
for this single-recipient instruction; CR 615.7 remains an independent gap.

### Exact support, engine contract and boundaries

Supported RON shape:
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, modifications,
ForAsLongAsPermanentRemainsTapped(ThisPermanent))/3`. The duration constructor
has exactly one symbol operand. It must bind to the permanent source of the
resolving ability. Existing source, host and local single-permanent target
subjects and temporary modifications are reused. Supported contexts are
resolving permanent activations and existing supported permanent triggers.
Spell-only, static, cost, collection-layer, non-source-duration operands and
control-duration forms remain rejected. `UntilEndOfTurn` remains supported.

`ron.compileTemporaryDuration` validates spelling, arity, symbol role and source
scope, then lowers to
`mage.UntilSourceUntaps(This, modifications ...ContinuousModification)
ResolvingEffect`. Typed permanent target plans and per-factory bindings remain
unchanged. Definition validation checks the duration's battlefield source and
all captured target reads; deleting a declaration makes the definition invalid.
Inventory reports the duration operand as `permanent_reference` only within a
known duration context and does not claim unsupported parent actions work.

The engine extends the existing `untilEffect` and `composedLayerEffect` capture
and layer installation services. A duration starts only while its original
source incarnation is present, phased in and tapped at resolution. Untapping
then retapping before resolution can start the duration; an absent, returned,
phased or untapped source installs nothing. After installation, actual untap,
source departure or source phasing ends it permanently. `EffectManager` owns
expiration flags; single and simultaneous untap services and `Game.PhaseOut`
record expiration at the transition, before untap notifications or a possible
retap/phase-in. Each installed layer has a clone-local expiration flag.
Indirect source phasing is included.

Subjects and values use existing capture semantics. Target phasing suspends
application without ending a source-dependent duration. Source expiration
while the target is phased still ends it. Returned targets receive no old bonus.
End-of-turn cleanup, source control changes and source ability removal do not
end the installed duration. A stun counter replacing untap leaves it active.
The new service does not adopt the legacy target-dependent auto-untap policy:
the separate printed permission to remain tapped is still a choice after the
target leaves. Existing callers are preserved.

This slice includes a missing reusable engine lifetime contract and its compiler
adapter. Existing layer ordering, declaration validation, target announcement
and rechecks, transactional costs, source/target incarnations, stack copies,
untap replacements and cloning supply the rest. Rules read: CR 611.2a–d,
702.26b–g and the existing identity/control-phasing contracts. No RON source
changed and no new data defect was found. Gaea's Liege and Fastbond observations
remain open. No Go definition or DSL function was removed; collection loading,
test migration and startup gates remain unmet. No deletion caller audit is
claimed.

### Exact contract, reuse and boundaries

Supported event signature/context:
`TriggerA(WhenAPermanentBecomesTapped(And([IsLandType(subtype),
ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)])), actions)` on a permanent.
`WhenAPermanentBecomesTapped/1`, `And/1` with a two-element list,
`IsLandType/1` with a symbol, and `ControlledByAPlayer/1` with symbol `Opponent`
are required. The two conjunction elements can appear in either order. Only
known engine land subtypes are accepted, with existing `subtypeName` conversion.
Duplicate, absent or additional filters, unknown/incorrect subtype families,
wrong argument kinds/arity, `Or`, different controller selectors and
`SinglePermanent` forms remain errors. Static, cost and spell-rule contexts
retain their existing rejection behavior.

`ron.compileOpponentLandTap(Node)` returns
`(func(mage.Effect) *mage.GenericTriggered, error)`. RON owns syntax and context
validation. It reuses `ValidateSubtypeFamily` and the existing event definition
validator to reject invalid event subtypes at compilation. The temporary
validation object is discarded; it is not registered or used for execution.
The returned plan captures only an immutable subtype string. Each card factory
builds a new event pattern and the existing per-instance trigger action plan.
There is no Go-card fallback, mutable shared target state, card-name branch,
game-time declaration panic, global action-result slot or partial registry.

Engine reuse: `OpponentLandBecomesTapped().OfSubtype`, `WhenEvent`, `Sequence`,
existing trigger action/target builders, APNAP queueing, clone/copy services,
transactional casting, mana taps and simultaneous `TapEach`. `GainLife` retains
the resolving trigger controller. Event matching uses current land type,
subtype and controller; pending triggers retain their event controller.
Departure/return and later control changes cannot redirect the gain. Phased
sources/lands cannot produce a matching event. No event permanent/player
binding is declared, so unbound `Trigger_ThatPermanent`/`Trigger_ThatPlayer`
reads remain errors. No permanent characteristic LKI read, replacement-order
change or new batch operation is introduced. Existing engine services own
those contracts. Rules read: CR 603.1–603.3, 603.2e and 701.26a/b.

provides a fresh `*mage.PermanentBinding` for each factory call.
`compilePermanentRef` lowers its event kind with `mage.From`. Each event pattern
and body are built together, including existing per-instance target builders.
No mutable chosen state is stored in the plan.

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse

Supported resolving action signature:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(CombatDamageWouldBeDealt, [PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
`CreatePreventDamageUntil/3` must be a positional tuple. The event and duration
must be the exact symbols above. The second argument must be a one-element list
containing the exact symbol `PreventThatDamage`. The compiler rejects empty or
multiple operations, extra effects, tuple spellings of symbols, other events,
other durations, wrong arity and cost/static/top-level rule contexts.
The existing resolving action compiler can use this shape in spell or activation
bodies. No reference or result is produced; no scope can read a prevention result.

`compileGlobalCombatPrevention(n Node) (effectFactory, error)` owns only RON
syntax, declaration diagnostics and lowering. Each build returns a fresh
`mage.PreventAllCombatDamage()` effect. The shared engine installs an independent
end-of-turn `fogReplacement` through `Game.SetPreventCombatDamage`. Existing
`ActionList`/`Sequence`, trigger/counter costs, casting transactions, cloning,
stack copies, combat batches, damage source services, replacement ordering and
cleanup own execution. There is no new engine rule, parallel damage system,
source lifetime, recipient binding, Go-card fallback, card-name branch,
global action-result slot, declaration panic or partial production registry.

Prevention starts at resolution, never at declaration or payment. It applies
to all combat damage for either player, first-strike and normal damage steps,
new sources and later combats in the same turn. It remains after its source
leaves, returns, phases or changes controller. Noncombat damage stays legal;
cleanup ends the effect. Copies can install the effect without repaying costs;
a countered spell installs nothing. No characteristic/controller LKI query,
finite shield allocation or new simultaneous operation is introduced.
Rules read: CR 514.2, 615.1–615.4, 615.6, 615.7, 615.12 and 616.1–616.1f.

This is a missing compiler adapter, not an engine or environment defect.
No selected source-data defect was found. Gaea's Liege and Fastbond observations

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

RON resolving action:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByCreature(ref), [PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
Both constructors require exact positional tuple arity. The operation list must
contain exactly the symbol `PreventThatDamage`; the duration must be exactly
the symbol `UntilEndOfTurn`. `ref` uses existing `compilePermanentRef` scope
validation: source, attachment, declared target or matching event references
only in their valid scopes. Unbound, incompatible, tuple-spelled and numbered
undeclared references remain errors. Cost/static/top-level rule contexts reject
the action. Filtered source sets and other events/durations remain unsupported.

`compileCombatPrevention(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` owns spelling,
validation and typed lowering. Each factory invocation builds fresh bindings.
`mage.PreventCombatDamageByThisTurn(PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` adds an explicit
end-of-turn constructor to the existing `combatSourcePreventionInstallation`.
Existing `PreventCombatDamageBy` and `PreventCombatDamageByEach` callers keep
end-of-combat duration. No DSL export alias was needed. The shared replacement
captures permanent ID and incarnation at resolution and uses existing damage
source snapshots, replacement ordering, cloning and cleanup. No parallel damage
system, mutable global result, card-name branch, declaration panic or production
registry exception was added. The implement-engine skill supplied the reusable
engine workflow; RON card definitions did not change.

Prevention starts only on resolution, lasts through later combats, and prevents
combat damage by the captured object to players/permanents. Damage to that
object and noncombat damage remain legal. Return gives a new incarnation;
phasing and controller changes do not change captured identity. Captured damage
from the old source after departure remains prevented. The creature target
filter is checked at announcement and resolution; it is not a dynamic filter
on every later source packet. Cleanup expires the replacement. Copied abilities
and spells use existing engine services and do not repay costs.

The gap was an engine duration constructor plus compiler adapter. No new source
data defect or environmental failure was found. Open earlier data observations
remain open. All twelve RON source hashes match baseline; no vocabulary snapshot
refresh is required. Runtime cutover/removal gates remain unmet. No Go card,
generator or DSL function was deleted; no deletion audit is claimed.

### Contract and implementation boundary

Exact supported shape:
`TargetPermanent(ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You)))`, either alone or inside
nested `And` with existing filters and `Other(ThisPermanent)`. Both constructors
require exact positional tuple arity and `You` must be a symbol. Available in
supported spell, mode, activation and trigger target declarations. Opponent,
owner, event-player, other player expressions, numbered/unbound player reads,
malformed forms and disjunctions containing this restriction remain errors.
Static, collection, cost, action and rule contexts retain their own contracts.

`compilePermanentTargetFilter(Node, scope)
(mage.PermanentFilter, []mage.PermanentTargetOption, error)` replaces its former
single source-exclusion boolean with immutable declaration options. Nested
conjunctions accumulate restrictions and characteristic filters. `compileTarget`
uses these options when each instance builds its fresh target declaration.
The new adapter calls `mage.TargetYouControl()`. Existing source exclusion calls
`mage.TargetOtherThanSource()`. All callers of the private compiler function were
audited; they are `compileTarget` and its recursive filter call. No exported DSL
function or engine service changed. No runtime state, global action slot,
card-name branch, fallback, partial registry or declaration panic was added.

The engine's existing target legality uses the stack controller at announcement
and resolution. Source control changes and departure do not change that
controller. Ownership is independent. Before resolution, recipient control
changes can make a target illegal; after resolution they do not end its bonus.
Targets preserve incarnation identity and phasing follows existing rules.
Costs retain transactional payment and rollback. Copies and cloned games retain
separate pending target context. Ashnod's Battle Gear also retains its exact
+2/-2 effect, optional untap choice and source-tapped lifetime, including lethal
toughness reduction. No new replacement or simultaneous-operation contract was
needed for this adapter; existing services remain in use.

Gap classification: missing compiler adapter, with exact engine behavior already
available. No new source-data defect or environment failure was found. The
prevention engine identity defect observed during candidate investigation stays
open for that later slice. Existing Gaea's Liege/Fastbond observations stay open.
All twelve RON hashes match the vocabulary snapshot; no source changed and no
snapshot refresh is required. Runtime cutover/removal gates remain unmet. No
Go card, generator, DSL export or engine function was deleted; no deletion caller
audit is claimed. Authoring cutover instructions remain for their gated phase.

### Supported signatures, contexts and implementation

Exact action:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(Or([CombatDamageWouldBeDealtToRecipient(Permanent(r)),
CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByCreature(r)]), [PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
`CreatePreventDamageUntil/3`, `Or/1`, both event constructors `/1` and
`Permanent/1` require positional tuples. `Or` takes exactly two list elements,
one event of each kind, in either order. Both event references must identify
the same `permanentReferencePlan`, including its lexical target/event identity.
Existing scoped symbols `Ref_TargetPermanent`, `ThisPermanent`, `HostPermanent`
and `Trigger_ThatPermanent` can be reused. The latter two require an Aura/event
scope. Different references, duplicate events, other unions, malformed wrappers,
player/numbered/unbound reads, other operations and durations remain errors.

Supported resolving contexts are existing single-target spells, modes,
activations and trigger bodies, including source/host and saved host-tap event
references. Cost, static layer and static `PreventDamage` contexts remain errors.
`compileCombatPreventionUnion(Node, scope) (permanentReferencePlan, error)` is
private to `ron`. It creates no game state. `compileCombatPrevention` builds
`mage.PreventCombatDamageToAndBy(PermanentRef)` through fresh instance bindings.
The inventory now assigns union descendants prevention-event/recipient/reference
roles; support and behavior fields remain unverified/report-only.

by captured source ID **and incarnation**, without requiring a live source.

also stops a shield on a new incarnation from matching damage from the old one.

source from installing a shield on a returned permanent; a regression test

### Exact signatures, dependencies and engine reuse

- `PermanentRuleEffect/2`, in the existing top-level permanent rule context,
  accepts `[CantBeBlockedExceptByDefenders(filter)]` with exactly one operation.
- `CantBeBlockedExceptByDefenders/1` must be a positional tuple. Its operand uses
  the existing `compileFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)` grammar,
  including nested `And`/`Or`, subtype, type, color and keyword filters. The
  operation's word `Defenders` means blockers, not the defender keyword.
- Subjects are bare `ThisPermanent` on a permanent and bare `HostPermanent` on
  an Aura. Target, event, numbered, malformed and nonpermanent references remain
  rejected in this static shape. Multiple operations and new temporary,
  collection or source-dependent filter contexts remain unsupported.
- `compilePermanentBlockingRule(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)` delegates
  other shapes to the retained self-untap compiler. Each factory constructs a
  fresh static `While` rule and builds a typed source/attachment reference.
- New engine API:
  `CantBeBlockedExceptBy(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter) ContinuousModification`.
  It extends `layerModification`/`capturedModification` and delegates to
  `EffectManager.AddCantBeBlockedExceptBy`. It installs a rules restriction,
  not a keyword on the subject. `While` reads current source/host membership;
  `Until(EndOfTurn, ...)` captures the recipient incarnation. Existing
  `SourceCantBeBlockedExceptBy`/`TargetCantBeBlockedExceptBy` callers remain.
- `cloneEffectManager` now copies `cantBeBlockedExceptByRules` and each filter
  slice. Before this repair, immediate clone queries lost active filtered
  restrictions until another layer pass. The immutable filter declarations
  remain shared; the map and slices are independent. This repair is limited to
  this filtered-attacker map, not a claim about every other computed map.
- Inventory assigns the operation operand `permanent_filter`, including nested
  descendants of unsupported enclosing records. Reporting is not gameplay proof.

declaration panic or partial production registry was added.

### Supported signature and reuse boundary

`TriggerA/2` accepts
`AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep/1(SinglePlayer/1(HostController))` on an Aura.
The event, selector and outer rule are positional tuples; `HostController` is
a bare symbol. The body uses the existing action-list/target compiler with a
local `stepEventPlan`. `Trigger_ThatPlayer` resolves through that plan's fresh
`PlayerBinding`. Sibling abilities cannot read the event binding.

The changed function is
`compileBoundStepTrigger(Node, Node, scope, mage.TurnStepPattern,
 mage.TurnStepPattern, string) (optionFactory, error)` in `end_step.go`.
Existing AnyPlayer/You upkeep and end-step callers remain supported. The new
branch is limited to the upkeep label and Aura context. Each factory invocation
constructs `AttachedControllerUpkeep(BindPermanent("upkeep host"), player)`.
The event's internal host capture is not exposed as `Trigger_ThatPermanent` and
does not override `HostPermanent` in the body.

Engine reuse: `AttachedControllerUpkeep`, native event matching,
`TurnStepBegins`, `BindPermanent`, `BindPlayer`, `FromPlayer`, pending trigger
captures, stack copying, `AttachedPermanent` and attachment LKI, permanent
incarnations, `DealDamageFrom`, prevention, `AddCountersTo`, Aura static P/T
layers, transactional casting/target services, and native upkeep priority.
No new engine API, parallel execution service, card-name branch, mutable chosen
state shared by factories, global last-action slot, fallback or partial
production registry was added.

The host controller is checked at detection; the event player then remains
fixed. Host control and Aura control are distinct. A counter instruction on
`HostPermanent` reads the current attachment at resolution. The departed source
uses its last attachment; a returned Aura or host cannot substitute its new
incarnation. Phased hosts receive no counter, while a phase cycle retains
identity. Source ability removal before detection suppresses the trigger;
removal after detection does not cancel it. Damage retains the captured player
and goes through prevention after source departure.

constructor `mage.ControlAttached` to its effect builders. Each factory builds

current Aura controller, not from a resolving spell context.

control from the old attachment, including before SBAs remove the invalid Aura.
A fresh legal attachment records the new incarnation. This is a reusable engine
identity repair, not a RON identity workaround.

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Public engine signatures remain:

```go
BecomesBasicLandsEffect(filter PermanentFilter, subtypes ...string) ContinuousEffect
BecomesBasicLandAttachedEffect(subtypes ...string) ContinuousEffect
AttachedEffect(layer Layer, apply AttachedApplyFunc) ContinuousEffect
```

The collection effect supports a pure filter and a fixed nonempty list drawn
from Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain and Forest. It selects current unphased
lands once per application. Input subtype slices are copied. Existing
`applyBecomesBasicLand`/`applySetSubtypes` execute CR 305.7: replace the land
subtype family and printed/copied rules-text abilities, retain other types,
supertypes and subtype families, and supply intrinsic mana. Separate grants
remain. Existing invalid constructor declarations still fail at construction;
no game-time declaration panic is added.

Private `basicLandSetEffect.selection(*Game) []uuid.UUID` orders live membership
for comparison. `DependsOn(ContinuousEffect, *Game) bool` probes the other
layer-4 effect on a clone and detects membership changes. The existing printed
ability wrapper also detects source-rule suppression in layer 4.
`probeContinuousEffect(ContinuousEffect, *Game) *Game` initializes separate
transient animation membership and uses the existing stateful-effect clone
contract. It performs no live writes. Pure filters and effect callbacks must
keep writes in their supplied game, as required by existing effect services.

The shared layer 3–6 executor reevaluates dependency order after each applied
effect and drops effects whose abilities no longer exist. The dependency graph
ignores only edges within the same strongly connected loop; dependent effects
outside the loop still wait. Original timestamp order remains the tie-breaker.
Index-based ordering avoids requiring comparable effect implementations.
No new CDA or layer-7 reevaluation contract is claimed.

Generic `AttachedEffect` checks the source's saved host incarnation in activity
and application. A host that leaves and returns cannot receive the old effect.
A new `Game.Attach` records the new incarnation. Phasing retains that identity;
a directly phased source suspends its static effect. Static effects use live
objects and do not substitute LKI for an absent host.

RON spelling, scopes and compiler plans are unchanged. `SetLandType/1` and
`SetLandTypeVariable/1` remain errors in every context. The next adapter must
lower static host and global forms to these services, then provide complete
RON gameplay coverage. No card-name branch, Go-card fallback, global result
slot, runtime registry cutover, new payment/replacement service, or DSL removal
is introduced. Simultaneous damage, replacement ordering and cost rollback
remain with existing services; this slice does not add those operations.

### TDD and evidence

Initial fixture issues (color/supertype names, Aura land filter, player getter)
were corrected. The first engine suite then failed on the intended missing
dependency detector, wrong timestamp result, stale remaining order and returned
host identity. The printed-effect existence test also failed before its repair.
A later loop-dependent test failed before the graph repair. The original loop
fixture had only one matching subtype and did not form a loop; it was corrected
to contain both subtypes. No behavior assertion was weakened.

A broad check exposed a dependency trial panic because `Game.Clone` omits the
transient animation map; the probe now supplies a separate map. The grant test
fixture also needed its normal absent-target check during phasing. Two retained
fixtures assigned `AttachedTo` without the saved incarnation: engine clone and
Tangle Kelp. Their setup now calls `Game.Attach`; assertions and scenarios stay.
These were implementation/fixture failures, not environment failures.

### Exact supported shapes and engine reuse

Capability `STATIC-OPPONENT-CONTROLS`: permanent rule
`If(APlayerPassesFilter(Opponent, ControlsA(filter)), [layer_rules...])`.
`APlayerPassesFilter/2` requires symbol `Opponent` and `ControlsA/1`.
`Opponent` has role `player_filter`, not `player_reference`; the other argument
has role `static_player_filter`. Nested filter descendants have role
`permanent_filter`. No opponent binding or mutable choice is introduced.

Static condition permanent filters add symbol `IsNonToken`, lowered to
`mage.Not(mage.IsToken)`. Nonempty recursive `And/1(list)` and `Or/1(list)`
now build these filters in the static-condition adapter. This also applies to
existing controller `ControlsA`/`ControlsNo` conditions. General target,
collection and resolving-action filter support is unchanged. Existing card-type,
subtype, color, supertype and tap/combat predicates retain their syntax limits;
ability/P/T queries stay rejected. Other player selectors, target/event/chosen
reads, invalid arities, tuple `IsNonToken()`, empty conjunctions, `ControlsNo`
on the opponent form and unsupported body/mixed-layer shapes remain errors.

Bodies reuse the complete existing single-layer contract: fixed `AdjustPT/2` or
nonempty `AddAbility/1` with existing supported keywords, on source/Aura host
or existing static collections. Ivory Guardians reuses
`IsNamed(NamedCard("Ivory Guardians"))` without a controller restriction.
No game-time declaration panic, card-name execution branch or fallback exists.

New shared API: `mage.OpponentControls(mage.PermanentFilter) mage.StateCondition`.
It uses the context controller's current opponent, requires a valid controller,
and reads unphased current battlefield membership. It uses the same
`GetOpponent`, `AnyBattlefield`, `And` and `ControlledBy` services as the existing
`WhileOpponentControls` source condition. It works with `While`, `IfState` and
other state-condition consumers and holds only an immutable filter. No engine
state, global result slot or alternate layer implementation is introduced.

Reuse: `While`, `Static`, `ModifyPT`, `ModifyEachPT`, `GrantKeywordModification`,
`MatchingPermanents`, `Named`, typed `This`, permanent incarnation and existing
protection/zone/control/layer/clone services. Each factory creates fresh static
rules/modifications. Layer 2 control, layer 4 types and layer 5 colors precede
bonuses in layer 7c. Ability removal in layer 6 disables the source bonus.
Membership remains live and uses no LKI. Phasing suspends the source/qualifier;
returning a card supplies its new controller and incarnation.
No payment, replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation contract is changed.

### Exact shapes, contexts and reuse

Permanent static rule `PermanentRuleEffect/2` accepts exactly one operation:

- `PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent, [CantBlockAttackers(filter)])`.
  `ThisPermanent` is a symbol and uses the typed source reference. Lower to a
  fresh `WithStaticAbility(SourceCanBlockOnly(Not(filter)))` per factory.
  Aura hosts, target, event and other subjects are rejected in this form.
- `PermanentRuleEffect(subject, [CantBeBlockedByDefenders(filter)])`.
  Subject is symbol `ThisPermanent` or Aura-only symbol `HostPermanent`.
  Lower to existing `Static(While(condition,
  CantBeBlockedExceptBy(subject, Not(filter))))`. The always-true condition and
  typed source/attachment selection reuse the established static blocking adapter.

Both operations have arity 1 and use the existing `compileFilter` grammar,
including recursive `And/Or`, type, subtype, color, keyword, tap/combat predicates
and fixed power comparisons. `PowerIs/1` accepts `GreaterThanOrEqualTo/1`,
`LessThanOrEqualTo/1` or `EqualTo/1`, whose argument is `Integer/1` with an integer
literal. Dynamic X and malformed declarations remain rejected. No filter
meaning is inverted globally: only the two prohibitions lower their filter
through `mage.Not`. `Defenders` denotes candidate blockers, not the defender
keyword. Existing `CantBeBlockedExceptByDefenders` semantics are unchanged.
Resolving-action, temporary, mixed operation lists and other static contexts
remain unsupported. Inventory now assigns their filter descendants the existing
permanent-filter, power-comparison, value, subtype and color roles independently
of whether another rule rejects the card.

Reuse: `SourceCanBlockOnly`, `CantBeBlockedExceptBy`, `Not`, `Static`, `While`,
`compilePermanentRef`, `compileFilter`, `HasPowerGTE/LTE/Equal`, current layers,
attachment/incarnation services, `CanBlock`, native blocker declaration and
combat damage, cleanup and ability-removal services. No new public API,
parallel combat rules, choice state, targets, global result slot, game-time
panic, card-name execution branch or Go fallback is introduced.

Only new engine behavior: clone the computed `canBlockOnlyRules` map and its
filter slices, alongside the existing attacker restriction map. Filters remain
immutable declarations. The shared engine owns clone state; RON owns spelling,
shape validation and lowering.

Static source rules stop on ability removal or phasing. Source return constructs
a fresh rule for its new incarnation and controller. Aura rules read the current
attachment; host ability removal does not remove the Aura's rule, and a returned
host does not inherit it. Static membership needs current objects and uses no
LKI. Filters read final characteristics at the block legality query. Existing
blocks persist after later filter changes (CR 509.1b). No replacement ordering,
simultaneous operation, trigger LKI or payment contract is changed. Native casting
and Veteran's activation exercise existing payment rollback and timing.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Permanent static rule `PermanentRuleEffect/2` accepts exactly one operation:

- `PermanentRuleEffect(subject, [CanAttackAsThoughItDidntHaveDefender])`.
- `PermanentRuleEffect(subject, [CanAttackAsThoughItHadHaste])`.

Each operation is a symbol, with no arguments. `subject` is symbol
`ThisPermanent` or Aura-only symbol `HostPermanent`. Wrong subjects/types,
unbound target references, tuple spellings, operation arguments, multiple
operations, collection rules and temporary/action contexts remain rejected.
This does not claim support for the whole permanent-rule family.

RON owns spelling, arity, scope validation and lowering. Typed permanent plans
are built through the existing instance services; each factory constructs a
fresh static action and modification. Existing `Static`, `While`, reference,
attachment, continuous-effect, ability-removal, cloning, incarnation, attack
legality, native declaration and casting services own runtime behavior.
The defender permission reuses `GrantKeywordModification(ref, AttrCanAttack)`.

Missing engine contract: attack-only haste. New public signature:
`AttackAsThoughHaste(subject PermanentRef) ContinuousModification`.
It installs a rule permission, not the haste ability. `CanDeclareAsAttacker`
reads it alongside full haste. `CanTapForEffect` retains its existing check, so
summoning-sick tap-cost activations remain illegal. The internal capability is
`core.AttrAttackAsThoughHaste`, appended without renumbering existing attrs.
`IsKeywordAttr` and `IsAbilityAttr` exclude it; copying or removing recipient
abilities cannot treat it as haste. No new mutable state service is needed.

Both rules retain tapping and independent attack restrictions. Static host
membership reads the current attachment and does not use LKI. Phasing suspends
source rules; host/source phase cycles restore current membership. Source ability
removal stops a static permission. Recipient ability removal does not remove a
permission supplied by an Aura. Control changes do not change its attachment.
A returned source needs a new attachment; a returned host does not inherit an
old attachment or captured temporary rule. A declaration already made remains
in combat after the permission ends. `Until` uses the existing incarnation
capture service; its cleanup and clone isolation remain shared engine behavior.

Complete local Oracle text in `data/LEA.json` confirms the two RON records:
Animate Wall ignores defender for attacking; Instill Energy ignores control
history for attacking and has the separate zero-mana untap restricted to its
controller's turn and once each turn. CR 609.4 limits an as-though effect to its
stated operation; CR 702.10b/c separates haste's attack and cost permissions.
There is no source-data defect in this slice. Existing Gaea's Liege/Fastbond
concerns remain outside it. No RON source changes or vocabulary refresh are needed.

No replacement ordering, simultaneous operation, event LKI, new payment,
saved result, global state slot, card-name execution branch, Go fallback, or
partial production registry is introduced. Existing callers are preserved.
No removal gate is met, so no Go definitions, generators or DSL functions are
removed, and no removal caller audit or authoring cutover is claimed.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil/3`, in resolving action context, accepts a
single operation and symbol `UntilEndOfTurn`:

- Symbol `CanAttackAsThoughItDidntHaveDefender`.
- Symbol `CanAttackAsThoughItHadHaste`.
- Tuple `CantBeBlockedByDefenders/1` with the existing permanent filter grammar.

The new forms accept symbol `ThisPermanent` on a permanent or a declared,
typed `Ref_TargetPermanent`. Activation, spell, mode-local and entry-trigger
resolving bodies are tested. Hosts, event/loop references, unbound or incompatible
subjects, multi-operation lists, tuple attack spellings, malformed filters and
other durations stay rejected. The existing `CantBeBlocked` shape retains its
target-only contract and existing callers/tests. This does not support the
whole temporary permanent-rule family or change static rules.

RON owns syntax/scope validation and lowering, and constructs modifications
with each factory's `instanceBindings`. Runtime behavior reuses `mage.Until`,
`GrantKeywordModification(ref, core.AttrCanAttack)`, `AttackAsThoughHaste(ref)`,
and `CantBeBlockedExceptBy(ref, Not(filter))`. No engine contract is missing;
no engine source or broad DSL export is changed. Attack-only haste remains a
rule permission, not full haste. Each rule captures the subject at resolution.
Current blocker filters, target legality, control/phase changes, returned-object
exclusion, payment rollback, cloned games and copied targets use shared services.
Replacement ordering, simultaneous operations and event LKI are not applicable
to the added adapters; no new contract for them is claimed.

### Exact contract and reuse

Internal signature:
`(*Game).damageFilterSource(uuid.UUID, DamageSource) *Permanent`.
`damagePreventionRuleReplacement.Matches(Action, GameReader) bool` uses it for
all three existing source-filter contexts: permanent recipients, explicitly
scoped player recipients, and source-only player rules.

Public APIs remain `Game.AddDamagePreventionRule`, `WithFrom`, `WithTo`,
`WithToPlayer`, and `PreventDamageFromTo`. No signature or declaration spelling
changes. The future RON adapter owns RON syntax and scope, and can reuse those
engine services. No new RON shape is claimed by this prerequisite slice.

A captured battlefield source has an ID and incarnation. The same present
incarnation supplies current characteristics, including changes made after
capture. A phased incarnation supplies a copy of its retained permanent.
A departed incarnation supplies a copy of `ZoneSystem.LKIByIncarnation`'s
snapshot. Ordinary LKI cleanup does not erase that incarnation map. A returned
card, including a later departure, cannot substitute for the original source.
Invalid IDs/incarnations and captured spell sources do not fall back to live
permanent lookup. Actions without captured source state retain UUID-only
compatibility. Filters must read the supplied permanent, rather than look up
its ID again. Pure callbacks remain the caller's contract.

Reuse: existing `DamageSource`, `CaptureDamageSource`, `clonePermanentInto`,
incarnation LKI storage, `DamageToPlayerAction`/`DamageToCreatureAction` source
metadata, redirection, amount-copy methods, simultaneous damage batches,
replacement choice/rechecking and cloned effect state. No parallel replacement,
zone, binding, payment or damage system is introduced. Recipient identity,
spell-source/general-source filtering, finite prevention allocation, protection
and the separate color/type prevention services remain outside this slice.

The earlier rules-contract section described this behavior, but the baseline
implementation still had three `FindPermanent(ActionSource())` lookups and none

and actual evidence, and corrects the stale test mapping. That documentation

### Exact supported context and reuse

Private adapter: `compileStaticPrevention(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
Supported top-level rule on a permanent:

```ron
PreventDamage(
    DamageWouldBeDealtByAPermanentToRecipient(
        source_filter,
        Permanent(ThisPermanent)
    ),
    [PreventThatDamage]
)
```

`source_filter` uses the existing validated permanent filter grammar, including
nested `And`/`Or`. The recipient uses `compilePermanentRef` and must have
`permanentSource` kind. Exactly one symbol operation is required. Invalid arity,
wrappers, operations, undeclared event/target references, host/player recipients,
spell rules and resolving-action contexts fail at compilation. Other static
prevention event shapes remain unsupported; no declarations panic during play.

Each factory creates a fresh static ability with
`mage.WithStaticAbility(mage.PreventDamageFromTo(from, mage.IsID))`.
The existing service binds the recipient to that ability's own battlefield
source. No mutable game state is captured by the compiler. The engine owns
continuous lifetime, ability removal, current characteristics, captured source
incarnation/LKI, phasing, clone state, damage packets and replacement ordering.
No engine API changes, parallel replacement services, global result slots,
card-name executor branches, Go factory fallbacks or production registries are
introduced. Fixture-only strict collections are tested; production keeps strict
whole-collection rejection.

Prevention covers all matching combat and noncombat damage repeatedly, without a
finite amount. It protects only the ability source, follows its controller and
phase cycle, and is installed afresh on a returned recipient. Ability removal
ends it. A present damage source supplies current characteristics; departed or
phased sources supply their captured incarnation data. A returned source does
not replace that data. Permanent filters do not match spell sources. Competing
redirection follows affected-player choice and rechecks recipient membership.
Costs and targets are unchanged and retain the previous engine contracts.

Inventory now assigns `PreventDamage` children to `prevention_event` and
`prevention_operation`, and assigns this event's children to `permanent_filter`
and `prevention_recipient`. Nested references keep `permanent_reference` roles.
This reporting change does not imply support for the rejected sibling shapes.
API and rules documentation describe only this shape and engine reuse.

### Exact supported shape, contexts, and reuse

Private compiler signature:
`compileMixedDamageRecipients(Node) (func() mage.DamageRecipientSet, error)`.

```ron
SpellDealsDamage(ThisSpell, amount,
    MultipleRecipients([EachPermanent(filter), EachPlayer(AnyPlayer)]))
PermanentDealsDamage(ThisPermanent, amount,
    MultipleRecipients([EachPermanent(filter), EachPlayer(AnyPlayer)]))
```

The two list members may appear in either order. Each member has arity one;
there must be exactly one of each. `filter` uses existing `compileFilter`
context-free permanent forms, including nested `And`/`Or` and flying tests.
`AnyPlayer` must be a symbol. No single player/permanent members, duplicate or
empty sets, player-history filters, nested unions, or unbound local/event/target
filters are admitted. Existing `compileInstanceValue` amount forms and source
checks remain in force. The damage action can appear in already-supported spell,
mode, activation, and trigger action builders; this slice adds no new envelope.
Real cards cover spell context; synthetic RON covers activation and entry-trigger
context with reversed member order. Unsupported static/cost contexts remain
errors through the existing role compilers.

RON owns spelling, shape validation, positioned diagnostics, and lowering.
Each effect build creates `DamageRecipients(EachPlayer,
MatchingPermanents(filter))`, passed to `DealDamageEach(This, recipients,
amount(bindings))`. The immutable filter carries no chosen game state. Existing
instance bindings supply values; no new target, result binding, global scratch
slot, card-name branch, Go fallback, or partial production registry is used.

The engine selects current recipients at resolution, captures their identities,
and processes one shared batch. Later entries and returned creatures qualify;
phased creatures do not. Current flying status supplies membership. Shroud does
not restrict a nontargeted collection. Damage still uses protection, prevention,
redirection, marked damage, player damage, and lifelink. Nonpositive amounts
produce no damage event. Notifications see the complete batch, and lethal
creatures leave at the state-based check after resolution. Death abilities then
resolve separately. Copied spells keep X; ability copies and game clones keep
original source incarnation/LKI and independent execution state.

Engine reuse: `DamageRecipients`, `EachPlayer`, `MatchingPermanents`,
`DealDamageEach`, `This`, existing resolution values, damage-source capture,
replacement/prevention pipeline, simultaneous damage outcomes, notification
batching, stack copies, transactional casting/activation, clone service, and
state-based actions. No missing engine contract was found for this exact shape.
Finite prevention across multiple source packets remains a separate contract.

Inventory assigns `MultipleRecipients/1` children in recipient context to
`recipient_set`, then `EachPermanent/1` to `permanent_filter` and `EachPlayer/1`
to `player_filter`. It walks rejected descendants without claiming support.
API/rules docs describe only the established adapter and inherited execution.

### Exact signatures, contexts, and ownership

Engine signatures:

```go
DamagePacketTo(DamageRecipientRef, ResolutionValue) DamagePacket
DealDamagePackets(DamageSourceRef, ...DamagePacket) ResolvingEffect
```

The packet stores typed immutable declarations. The action copies its input
slice, visits every packet in definition inspection, rejects empty/nil/unbound
declarations, and resolves one source and all positive recipient amounts before
submitting damage. Positive amounts for the same resolved recipient identity
are summed before replacement processing. Zero/negative packets do not create
an event or subtract another packet's amount. Stable first-recipient order is
retained. Existing `Game.DealSimultaneousDamage`, assignment constructors and
source/reference/value resolvers execute the instruction. No parallel damage
system, generic dispatch, scratch result slot or new replacement service exists.

RON private signatures:
`compileDamagePackets(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` and
`compileDamagePacketRecipient(Node, scope) (damageRecipientFactory, error)`.
Exact action shapes:

```ron
SpellDealsMultipleDamage(ThisSpell, [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient), ...])
PermanentDealsMultipleDamage(ThisPermanent, [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient), ...])
```

Both have arity two. The second operand is a nonempty list and each member is
exactly `DamageToRecipients/2`. The source must be the matching symbol in an
existing spell/permanent context. Amounts use `compileInstanceValue` unchanged.
Recipients are the in-scope symbol `Ref_AnyTarget`, `Player(ref)/1` using
`compilePlayerRef`, or `Permanent(ref)/1` using `compilePermanentRef`.
Existing scope, type, incarnation and binding requirements remain in force.
No plural recipient set, numbered/unbound target, opponent choice, malformed
wrapper or mismatched source is silently accepted. Each factory lowers fresh
packet effects against that action's `instanceBindings`. Existing spell,
activation, supported trigger and modal envelopes share this lowering; the slice
adds no envelope, target declaration, event binding, result or announcement rule.
Real cards cover spells and activations; synthetic RON covers player/permanent
wrappers in spells, activations and entry triggers. Modal envelope lowering is
reused without a new mode contract or additional real-card coverage claim.

Inventory now gives the action's packet operand role `damage_packet` and
`DamageToRecipients/2` children roles `value` and `recipient`. Existing wrappers
then provide player/permanent-reference roles. Descendants of still-rejected
records remain reported, with support explicitly unverified.

Reuse includes definition validation, per-factory targets, stack legality,
transactional casting/activation, stack copies and retargeting, clone isolation,
current source characteristics and retained incarnation LKI, phasing, damage
assignment/batches, protection/prevention/redirection, affected-player replacement
order, lifelink, planeswalker loyalty, and post-resolution state-based actions.
RON owns only spelling, shape/scope checks and lowering. No Go fallback,
card-name branch or partial production registry is introduced. Old callers stay
available. API and rules docs describe only this shape and inherited behavior.
